code_review.project_type: full-stack web application — FastAPI backend + React/Vite SPA gallery of AI-pattern example apps

existing_self_description.text: Built with Spec4 (BWS4) is a living showcase of common AI application patterns, presented as a collection of small, self-contained example apps behind a single landing page. Each example demonstrates one pattern end-to-end: how it's built, what it depends on, and how it behaves, so that visitors unfamiliar with the underlying technique can understand it by seeing it work rather than by reading about it abstractly.

architecture.summary: Monorepo pairing a vertical-slice FastAPI backend — one self-contained package per AI-pattern example app (rag, react, collab, planning, orchestrated, chained_calls, embeddings), each with schemas/service/runtime/validator layers and versioned Markdown prompts — with a shared services substrate for generation, embedding, web search, moderation and usage limits, fronted by a React SPA with per-example lazy-loaded route chunks.
architecture.pattern: vertical-slice (feature-sliced) layered monolith with shared services substrate

api_surface.summary: Liveness endpoint, kept independent of the embeddings warm-up
Serves the three A2A-shaped agent cards from module constants, serialised by alias in camelCase
Streams the six-stage negotiation as server-sent events with 15s keep-alive pings; session opened inside the generator
Runs exactly two chained model calls; a failed second call returns 200 with status critique_failed so call 1's output survives
Describes the chain's two roles before it runs, built from the same constants the pipeline executes

ai_capabilities.name: litellm
ai_capabilities.description: Every text-generation and tool-calling model call in the gallery goes through one shared registry that walks an ordered chain of free-tier models on failure and benches slugs a provider has withdrawn, routing to OpenRouter and Groq

ai_capabilities.name: pydantic-ai
ai_capabilities.description: Second model lane used where an app wants the framework to bind and validate typed output rather than parsing JSON out of prose; reads slugs from the same registry and passes the same usage-limit gate

ai_capabilities.name: sentence-transformers
ai_capabilities.description: Runs all-MiniLM-L6-v2 in-process to embed the 24 curated preset texts, visitor-supplied text, and every RAG chunk and query

ai_capabilities.name: torch
ai_capabilities.description: Inference runtime beneath sentence-transformers, loaded at boot in the FastAPI lifespan warm-up rather than lazily on first request

ai_capabilities.name: pgvector
ai_capabilities.description: Stores dataset chunk embeddings in a dataset_embeddings table with an HNSW index and serves cosine-distance retrieval through SQLAlchemy queries

ai_capabilities.name: in-project RAG pipeline
ai_capabilities.description: Hand-rolled sentence-aligned overlapping chunking with source titles prepended, retrieval of top passages, grounded answer generation, and post-hoc auditing of every citation against the passages actually retrieved

ai_capabilities.name: scikit-learn
ai_capabilities.description: PCA projection of embeddings to 2D for the embeddings example's scatter plot, fitted once at startup over the curated preset set and never re-fitted so existing points never move

ai_capabilities.name: Exa
ai_capabilities.description: Live web-search API exposed as a shared framework capability, used today as the function-calling tool in the tool-use app and as the act step of the ReAct loop

ai_capabilities.name: in-project agentic slices
ai_capabilities.description: Four hand-built agent patterns: planning agent (plan, human approval, then execute with budget accounting), orchestrated subagents (coordinator briefs two of four fixed specialists concurrently and merges answers), multi-agent A2A negotiation (fixed 8 model calls per run with structurally enforced opacity), and a ReAct loop (think/act/observe with duplicate-query refusal and verbatim observations)

ui_summary.styling: Tailwind CSS with class-based light/dark strategy; theme preference persisted to browser localStorage
ui_summary.routing: react-router router object in frontend/src/routes.tsx consumed by RouterProvider, with per-example lazy-loaded chunks and installSeo(router) for per-route titles, descriptions, canonicals and GA4 page views

quotes.value: double in Python, single in TypeScript

test_coverage.coverage_summary: Backend pytest suite at backend/tests with testpaths pinned there and pythonpath = ['.']; addopts = "-m 'not live'" deselects every test that reaches real model providers or real Exa, so the gating suite runs entirely on recorded fixtures and a green run says nothing about live provider behaviour. Frontend uses vitest with jsdom and Testing Library via `npm run test`. Per-slice test packages are implied by pyproject comments referencing backend/tests/react.

incomplete_or_dead_code: `uv run ruff check .` gates only code written from v5 onward: [tool.ruff] extend-exclude lists pre-v5 paths file by file (backend/app/main.py, most of backend/app/api/, much of backend/app/services/) where ruff reports 366 findings across 57 files, so a clean lint run does not mean the file you edited was linted.
mypy strict checking is scoped the same way — backend/app/api/collab.py notes the pre-v6 routers 'inherit an exemption', so a passing typecheck does not imply the module you edited is type-checked.
backend/app/react/prompts/.gitkeep remains alongside four real prompt files — leftover scaffolding from when the directory was empty.
No CI configuration exists anywhere in the tree despite pyproject.toml comments reasoning about what 'fails in CI', so the ruff/mypy/pytest gates are enforced only by developer discipline locally.

change_risks.risk: README states the per-capability free-tier chains 'both rot as providers retire free slugs, so expect to refresh them'; any code that names a specific model slug will break silently when a provider withdraws it
change_risks.mitigation_hint: resolve models through the registry's ordered chain and bench mechanism rather than hardcoding slugs; both the LiteLLM and PydanticAI lanes must read from that same registry

change_risks.area: streaming run endpoints (/api/collab/run and the planning/orchestrated equivalents)
change_risks.risk: these handlers deliberately do NOT use Depends(get_db_session) because the streaming response outlives the request scope; a new streaming endpoint that takes the session as a dependency will fail at runtime
change_risks.mitigation_hint: open the session inside the async generator via async_session_factory, as backend/app/api/collab.py does

change_risks.risk: ensure_built() is wrapped in a bare `except Exception` with `# noqa: BLE001` so a broken embeddings projection logs and boots anyway, moving the cost to the first request; adding initialization here that must not fail silently will be swallowed
change_risks.mitigation_hint: keep warm-up best-effort and idempotent; anything genuinely fatal belongs outside that try block or in an explicit health check

change_risks.risk: each agent's turn is assembled only from messages addressed to it, which is the demonstration's central claim (a seller cannot learn a rival's price even when prompted); a refactor of opacity.py or sequencer.py that widens the assembled message set breaks it invisibly
change_risks.mitigation_hint: preserve the per-recipient message assembly and the message-log assertion that there is no seller-to-seller traffic

change_risks.area: JSON Schema conformance in the single-call app
change_risks.risk: 2 of the 8 free models in the chain do not honour a schema directive; the app reports non-conformance with raw output rather than dressing it up as success, and 'fixing' this by coercing or retrying would erase the behaviour the example exists to show
change_risks.mitigation_hint: keep server-side validation failures surfaced verbatim rather than converted into an error or a silent retry

security_observations: Unauthenticated public API by design; abuse is bounded by per-UTC-hour and per-day usage caps enforced before any provider call (backend/app/services/allowance_holds.py, text_gate, migrations 0007/0009/0010) rather than by identity
CORS is pinned to exactly one origin from settings.cors_origin in backend/app/main.py, never '*'
Render secrets are marked `sync: false` in render.yaml so they are entered in the dashboard rather than committed
Browser localStorage holds theme preference only and is explicitly not treated as a source of truth
User-supplied text passes a Moderator dependency and moderation events are persisted (migration 0011_moderation_log)
other_notes: Frontend lint: `npm run lint` (oxlint, the Rust-based Oxc linter; no ESLint and no Prettier in the project)
Frontend preview of the production bundle: `npm run preview`
Alembic migrations are driven from `backend/alembic.ini` with env at backend/app/db/migrations/env.py
`.env.example` present at repo root; its contents were not sampled, so env var names above are drawn from source reads and README prerequisites and should be cross-checked against it
Every source file in both languages opens with a provenance header: `# Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai` / `// Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai`

Codebase convention: unusually heavy explanatory comments stating why a decision was made (CORS exposure policy block, lifespan docstring, collab router preamble, ruff exclusion rationale in pyproject.toml) — new code is expected to match this density
Each slice ships versioned Markdown prompt files under backend/app/<slice>/prompts/ (e.g. answer_v1.md and answer_v2.md) loaded through a prompt_loader.py rather than inline string literals
Recurring pattern: every slice post-audits its own model output — rag/citations.py, chained_calls/overlap.py, react/annotation.py, collab/opacity.py

render.yaml defines two targets: bws4-api (type web, runtime python, plan starter, region oregon, rootDir .) and a Render Static Site for the web client; the starter plan is chosen because the process loads torch and sentence-transformers and fits the PCA projection in lifespan, making free-tier spin-down cold starts the showcase's most visible rough edge
No Dockerfile, docker-compose, Kubernetes manifest, or Terraform exists in the tree
Plotly is pinned to the plotly-basic build (~1 MB rather than ~4.7 MB) and confined to the embeddings route's lazy chunk
README states adding a gallery app to the landing page, header menu, and router is a single entry in one file
CLA.md and CONTRIBUTING.md exist at repo root (contents not sampled)
File listing was truncated at 269 additional files, so backend/tests/ contents, frontend/src/ route modules, and any CI directory were not directly observed
